title: India Battle Complacency as Bangladesh Stand Between Them and Asian Games Final
excerpt: Defending champions India face Bangladesh in Sunday's women's semifinal at Nisshin with a gold-medal match berth — and an unblemished Asian Games knockout record — on the line.
body:
• India face Bangladesh in the women's cricket semifinal on Sunday, September 20 at 10:30 AM IST at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin, Japan.
  • India are defending Asian Games champions and have won 22 of 25 T20Is against Bangladesh, including a 40-run win in this month's Asia Cup semifinal.
  • Bangladesh reached the semifinal without playing their quarterfinal — their clash with China was washed out and they advanced on ranking.
  • World No. 1 T20I bowler Shree Charani has back-to-back four-wicket hauls; India's middle order remains the one untested area.

Favourites — but wary

On Sunday morning, India's women begin the defence of their Asian Games crown in earnest. The defending champions take on Bangladesh in the second semifinal of the women's cricket competition at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin, on the outskirts of Nagoya, with the match scheduled to begin at 10:30 AM IST. The winner meets the victor of the Pakistan–Sri Lanka semifinal in the gold-medal match on September 22.

India are overwhelming favourites — and that is precisely the danger. As Deccan Herald framed it, Harmanpreet Kaur's side must battle complacency as much as Bangladesh: anything less than a complete performance in a knockout match can unravel months of dominance.

"Left-arm spinner Shree Charani starred again with the ball, recording her second consecutive four-wicket haul, and has climbed to the top of the ICC T20I bowling rankings."

The road to the semifinal

The women's competition skipped a group stage entirely, jumping straight into an eight-team knockout bracket, with India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka seeded directly into the quarterfinals. India opened against hosts Japan on Friday and produced a ruthless display, bowling Japan out for 57 before chasing the target down with eight wickets in hand.

Left-arm spinner Shree Charani starred again with the ball, recording her second consecutive four-wicket haul, and has climbed to the top of the ICC T20I bowling rankings. Shafali Verma contributed with both bat and ball, Deepti Sharma delivered in both departments, fast bowler Nandani Sharma made a strong impression, and leg-spinner Shreyanka Patil picked up a wicket on her comeback from an injury layoff.

Bangladesh's path was entirely different. Their quarterfinal against China was washed out without a ball bowled after persistent rain in the Nagoya region, and they advanced by virtue of their higher ICC ranking. It is a mixed blessing: Bangladesh avoided the pressure of a knockout match but arrive at the semifinal with no competitive game time at the venue and no match rhythm.

A familiar mismatch — on paper

The history between these sides is lopsided. At the last Asian Games in Hangzhou, India thrashed Bangladesh in the semifinal — bowling them out for 51, with Pooja Vastrakar taking four wickets — before going on to win gold. Overall, India have won 22 of their 25 T20I meetings with Bangladesh and are riding a nine-match winning streak that began with that Hangzhou semifinal.

The gap was on display as recently as September 10, when India beat Bangladesh by 40 runs in the Asia Cup semifinal in Dubai. Bangladesh's batting has consistently been the weaker link against top Asian sides, though their bowling has shown solidity in patches.

Why India can't take it lightly

Knockout cricket has its own logic, and this Indian side has one genuine vulnerability: the middle order has seen limited match-pressure exposure, with the top order and bowlers handling most of the workload through the Asia Cup and the quarterfinal. If Bangladesh's bowlers strike early, untested batters will be walking into a semifinal cauldron.

Bangladesh also have motivation money can't buy. Captain Nigar Sultana Joty, the 29-year-old wicket-keeper batter, has confirmed she will step down from T20I captaincy once this tournament concludes — and she marked her 200th international appearance during the Asia Cup. A farewell upset against the team that has tormented her side would be the defining note of her tenure.

An Asian Games moment for cricket

Cricket's place at the Asian Games is still new — the sport returned to the quadrennial event at Hangzhou 2023 — and it forms part of cricket's broader push onto the multi-sport stage ahead of its return to the Olympics at Los Angeles 2028. For the Indian diaspora in Japan, small in number but growing, Sunday's semifinal is a rare chance to watch the world-beating women's side play on Japanese soil.

What's next

Sunday's winner advances to the gold-medal match on September 22, while the loser will contest the bronze-medal match the same day. India are chasing back-to-back Asian Games golds, and a victory would set up a title defence against either Pakistan or Sri Lanka. Indian viewers can watch the semifinal live on the Sony Sports Network, with streaming on the SonyLIV app and website.
